name: Kit Room
summary: A cricket club sign-in: the scoreboard counts runs as you type, a wrong password knocks the bails off
about: A full sign-in page for a Lahore cricket club, set in a locker room with navy lockers, a kit bench, floodlight beams and a big LED scoreboard. Every letter you type scores runs (an @ is a six, a dot is a four) and spins the padlock dial; the lights drop and open lockers slam shut for your password, and a wrong one flashes OUT, adds a wicket and sends the bails flying. Signing in hits a six, drops the padlock and swings locker 18 open to show your shirt.
how: Watch the page play a demo innings by itself, then click any field to take over
Type an email and watch the runs, overs and padlock dial move; try an @ for a six
Click the password: the lights dim and lockers slam; the eye button lets one floodlight back in
Try a wrong password for a wicket, or use Fill it in (zoya@kitroom.pk, coverdrive9) to open locker 18
On Join the club your name and number print on the shirt and each password rule is a good ball; reset code 418207
